decisions.reason: The title asserts uncut-test admissibility, contradicted by u=1, k=0 on B1: the positive truncation has nonzero trace. The Statement and proof correctly restrict unconditional H1-zero membership to compactly supported cutoff products, and retain the continuous-source-pairing caveat. Corrected only the title; chain-rule, ACL product, compact-support density and boundary-order interfaces were checked.

Without theta>0 the stated estimate is false: A=I, theta=-1, Ma=1, u=x1, f=0, k=0 and a nonzero cutoff in {x1>0} give a positive gradient integral and negative right side. Added 0<theta<=Ma^2 to Statement and Given. Matrix Cauchy-Schwarz yields cross term 2Ma S b; Young absorption gives precisely 4Ma^2/theta and 2/theta. Local L2 forcing and nonnegative-test density license the cutoff test; F1 now records the supplier AC hypothesis explicitly.

The original coefficient bounds admit A=0 and theta=0. In dimension three u=|x|^(-1/4) is nonnegative H1 on B2 (its squared gradient has radial integral proportional to integral r^(-1/2) dr), satisfies every zero-form test, but is unbounded at zero. Added 0<theta<=Ma^2 to Statement and Given. Reviewed convex power truncation subsolutions, dyadic energy normalization Z=R^(-n)T^(-2)Y, the n=2 delta=1/2 substitute, the finite radius-gap cover, monotone convergence for p>=2, and the uniformly bounded outer-radius interpolation for 0<p<2.

The change of variables g(y)=R^2 f(x0+Ry) gives ||g||q=R^(2-n/q)||f||q for every q, including q=n/2. Thus the dimensional assertion about q was false, although the estimate and strict integrability hypothesis are correct. Replaced it by the dilation identity and the boundedness qualification; retained the full estimate. Reviewed source-pairing extension via Sobolev/Holder, the real Lax-Milgram barrier, its nonnegativity and supremum bound from the principal zero-boundary maximum principle, the positive-part subsolution test, all p>0, and the zero-source branch.

The supplied weak-Harnack Statement gives C(n,q,theta,Ma,p), whereas the remark omitted q while retaining the source-dependent inequality. Added q and its Lq-source role. Checked the supplier proof: a source-removing barrier has a q-dependent maximum bound, the seed exponent depends on n and ellipticity, finitely many positive-integrability Sobolev transitions reach every p<n/(n-2) using input exponents below one, and smaller exponents follow by Holder. The n=2 finite-exponent exception and open endpoint remain intact.

The n>=3 finite-chain interface cannot license the explanation for this R2 witness; moreover it compares only compact connected positive-measure subsets, not all of Omega. The fatality threshold is not affected: steps 1.1 and 2.1 already prove the counterexample without that lemma, since u is H1 with zero weak gradient and sup=1, inf=0. Repaired F4 and step 3.1 to state the exact cited range and prove the no-chain obstruction directly by convexity of balls and finite induction. Qualified the explanatory paragraph, preserving the refuted claim and the two-dimensional witness.
